previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and prior strokes presented with acute onset nausea, vomiting, posterior headache, and imbalance. MRI confirmed an acute to subacute left cerebellar infarction. He was admitted to the neurology stroke service, briefly monitored in the ICU due to supratherapeutic INR and concern for swelling, but required no surgical intervention. His warfarin was held and later restarted, and aspirin was reduced to 81 mg to minimize bleeding risk. He showed clinical improvement in coordination and gait, was able to ambulate independently, and was discharged home on day four with outpatient physical therapy, medication adjustments including a switch to atorvastatin, and close follow-up for stroke prevention and diabetes management.

Brief Hospital Course:
#  Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation: Pt with weight 
gain, SOB, ___ edema.  He was given a 120 mg bolus of IV 
furosemide on admission and was started on a furosemide gtt (10 
mg/hr).  He is approximately 2 L negative over night.  His 
lactate was mildly elevated on admission and will be trended 
this morning.  Dry weight 115 kg.  He was treated with a 
furosemide gtt 10 mg/hr and metolazone 2.5 mg daily initially, 
but this was stopped on ___ in the setting of a rising 
lactate.  He also continued spironolactone and ramipril.  His 
BBlocker was initially held in the setting of an elevated 
lactate.  Patient was diuresed with bolus doses of IV Lasix 
(ultimately with sufficient urine output to 160mg IV Lasix), 
with electrolytes monitored during active diuresis. Afterload 
was reduced by further uptitration of home ramipril dose from 
1.25mg daily to 1.25mg BID. He was restarted on his home 
torsemide dose of 60mg BID, and was monitored for fluid status. 
The patient remained net even to slightly negative on Torsemide 
60mg BID, and as a result he was not restarted on his home 
metolazone while in-house, and was not instructed to restart 
this medication after discharge. 
 
# Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: INR on presentation 
supratherapeutic at 3.9. Rates controlled.  Warfarin initially 
held and INR trended daily.  The INR goal is ___. When patient's 
INR became therapeutic at 2.6, and at that time, his home dose 
of warfarin was initiated at 2.5mg daily. The patient's INR 
became subtherapeutic on ___ at 1.7, for which he was initiated 
on a Lovenox bridge, and his warfarin dose was increased to 3mg 
daily. He was discharged on Lovenox ___ and warfarin 3mg 
daily, and will continue to use Lovenox until his INR returns to 
therapeutic range.

# The patient was observed to have several prolonged runs of 
VTach (approx. 30 seconds x1 episode, and ___ seconds on 2 
other occasions). The patient's home metoprolol (fractionated to 
tartrate) was resumed at that time as the patient was no longer 
in decompensated heart failure and his lactate had normalized. 
Metoprolol was increased to XL 37.5mg at the time of discharge 
for a brief run of VT on ___ while on metoprolol XL 25mg. 

# Acute Kidney Injury: Baseline Cr 1.1. Cr on admission 1.3. 
Likely cardiorenal, given overall picture of acute on chronic 
CHF.  He was diuresed as above, his Cr was trended, and his 
medications were renally dosed. Cr gradually downtrended with 
further diuresis, and improvement in lactate.
